summary: Blue Knob, Bedford County: state steel tower built 1921, relocated 1951, removed 1991. Summit now in Blue Knob State Park; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with a glass-enclosed cab (register; 1941 survey)
facts.status_note: The register says it was removed in 1991. The summit now lies within Blue Knob State Park.

access.note: Blue Knob State Park land. Wikipedia says a park trail starts on the Tower Road just below the summit. No source describes the old tower site itself.

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forestry (1921), later Department of Forests and Waters; Blue Knob State Park since 1945

events.note: Steel tower erected in the summer of 1921 (June 1922 Gazette); register gives 1921 as the build year
Five fires reported in one batch near the tower in October; the Kane Republican said they appeared to be set
A blaze about five miles from the tower could not be seen for some time by the towerman
1928 notice refers to the towerman being on duty
Lower two flights of steps to be removed when the towerman is off duty, because of damage
National Geodetic Survey station description: about 75 feet, glass cab, Civil Aeronautics Bureau airway beacon on the roof
National Park Service transferred the land to Pennsylvania; it became Blue Knob State Park

evidence.supports: The August 1921 notice named Blue Knob as one of the first 18 towers to be put up
evidence.quote: One of the first 18 towers will be put up at Blue Knob, Bedford county.

evidence.supports: The June 1922 Gazette said fifty 60-foot steel towers had been erected in the latter part of summer 1921
evidence.quote: During the latter part of the summer of 1921, the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry erected fifty sixty foot steel towers.

evidence.supports: The October 1922 Mirror described the Blue Knob tower as sixty feet tall
evidence.quote: sixty foot steel fire tower erected on the very pinnacle of the mountains between Blue Knob and Pavia

evidence.supports: The 1922 Gazette gave the summit an elevation of 3,165 feet and called it the highest point in the state
evidence.quote: stands on the highest point in the state, an elevation of thirty-one hundred and sixty-five feet above sea level.

evidence.supports: The register: steel Aermotor tower built 1921, relocated 1951, removed 1991
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921, relocated in 1951 and removed in 1991.

evidence.supports: The register gives the elevation as 3,025 feet (922 m)
The October 1921 fires near the tower were reported in one batch and thought to be set
evidence.quote: Five fires in one batch were reported near the fire tower on Blue Knob, Bedford county, and there were evidences that all had been caused by incendiaries.

evidence.supports: The October 1922 blaze was about five miles from the tower
evidence.quote: The blaze started only about five miles from the fire tower on the top of Blue Knob

evidence.supports: A towerman could not see the 1922 blaze for some time
evidence.quote: but because of an unusual contour of the mountains it could not be seen for some time by the towerman.

evidence.supports: The tower was open to the public daily until December 1 (1922)
evidence.quote: which is open daily until Dec. 1, to the public.

evidence.supports: The state forestry department, later the Department of Forests and Waters, erected the tower (1924 notice)
evidence.quote: Some years ago the State Forestry Department - now the Department of Forests and Waters - erected a fine fire tower on the top of Blue Knob

evidence.supports: In 1928 the lower two flights of steps were to be removed when the towerman was off duty
evidence.quote: Because of the damage done to the Blue Knob tower, it has been decided that the lower two flights of steps will be removed from the tower when the towerman is not on duty.

evidence.supports: The damage included broken glass, locks and woodwork
evidence.quote: the loss in broken glass and locks and repairing woodwork has made the step necessary

evidence.supports: The 1941 survey gives the tower about 75 feet high
evidence.quote: IT IS A FOUR-LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE ABOUT 75

evidence.supports: The 1941 survey describes a glass-enclosed cab on top
evidence.quote: FEET HIGH WITH A GLASS-ENCLOSED CAB ON TOP.

evidence.supports: The 1941 survey describes an airway beacon of the Civil Aeronautics Bureau on the cab roof
evidence.quote: AERONAUTICS BUREAU ON THE ROOF OF THE CAB.

evidence.supports: The land was transferred to Pennsylvania in 1945 and became Blue Knob State Park
evidence.quote: On September 26, 1945, the National Park Service transferred Blue Knob to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and it became Blue Knob State Park.

evidence.supports: A park trail starts on the Tower Road just below the summit
evidence.quote: the trailhead can be found on the Tower Road just below the summit

evidence.supports: The Tower Road passes a gated road to Herman Point, which has transmitter towers on its summit
evidence.quote: proceed up the Tower Road and pass by the gated road which leads to Herman Point and the transmitter towers on its summit

sources.title: History of Blue Knob State Park

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 3,025 ft (922 m); a June 1922 Bedford Gazette piece gives 3,165 feet. Not resolved. The story reports both, and the record keeps the register figure.
1922 notices say sixty feet; the 1941 survey description says about 75 feet. The record keeps 18.3 m (60 ft) and the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Do not merge with us-pa-blue-knob, which is the Big Knob tower in Perry County. The Gazette's highest-point claim is reported as the paper's claim and not repeated as fact. The 1924 Altoona Tribune item about damage and fines concerns the Blue Ridge tower in the Buchanan Forest District, not Blue Knob, and was not used. The brief's Eastern coordinates (40.2886, -78.5614) do not appear in the page text; the register gives N 40.295354, W 78.573906. Access rests on Wikipedia's trail description, not a current site visit. Most history comes from one compiled page that quotes newspapers and an NGS datasheet. No photos found.
